issue_context.title: Any call to OSSL_ENCODER_CTX_new_byXXX needs to support passing a libctx.
issue_context.body:
This is related to some new encoder code that ignores the libctx:

e.g:
PEM_write_bio_Parameters() uses the macro IMPLEMENT_PEM_provided_write_body_vars()
which then calls
OSSL_ENCODER_CTX_new_by_##type(x, PEM_SELECTION_##asn1, "PEM", PEM_STRUCTURE_##asn1,  NULL, NULL);
The last 2 params are the libctx, propq which will not work if they are just NULL..

So we either need to extract the libctx (which doesnt address that there is no propq)..
using 
````
const OSSL_PROVIDER *prov = EVP_KEYMGMT_provider(pkey->keymgmt);
OSSL_LIB_CTX *libctx = ossl_provider_libctx(prov);
````
OR have a PEM_write_bio_Parameters_ex(libctx, propq) ??


To reproduce this locally do..
````
export OPENSSL_TEST_LIBCTX=1
apps/openssl genpkey -genparam -algorithm DSA
````

review_comments: There is no propq in the macro params?

Why should there be?  `IMPLEMENT_PEM_provided_write_body_vars()` implements the two variables `libctx` and `propq`, which the rest of the building blocks can use.  Why should the implementing macros need to specify those variables explicitly?
Just a personal style thing I guess.
That seems unnecessary, and potentially confusing...
Where is the libctx? It is in the macro def but not here.
